name: Centinela
tagline: Autonomous agent that watches Colombian public procurement and issues opportunities and red flags with cited evidence.

awards: Winner (only prize): USD 300 + 6 months of Croma

problem: Procurement risk and opportunity are invisible when contracts are read one at a time, and checking a supplier across registries takes weeks of integration work.
solution: Every two hours it checks new processes for flagged entities and contractors, chains six official sources (procurement, company registry, corporate supervisor, judiciary, disciplinary and fiscal-control records) and returns a verdict with the evidence chain; it spots cross-contract signals and drafts the freedom-of-information request, evidence dossier and social thread.
demo_moment: The same flagged process shown twice: as a winnable low-competition opportunity for a small business, and as a red flag (single bidder, two-month-old company) for a citizen.

why_it_stood_out.claim: One engine, two products: the paying SME opportunity feed funds the free citizen watchdog.
Finds patterns invisible contract-by-contract: award concentration around one supplier, shared legal representatives between supposed competitors.
Does not stop at the finding — drafts the legal information request and the dossier.
Autonomous: runs on a schedule without being asked, unlike the search/research tools most other entrants built.
Won from the most crowded lane (7 of 12 projects did procurement): differentiation came from autonomy, dual use and action, not topic choice.

lessons: In a crowded lane, compete on autonomy and the next action, not on better search.
Show the business model inside the demo: who pays, who benefits.
